body.question: On 30 June 1908, an explosion over Siberia flattened forest. About how many square kilometres?
body.reveal: The Tunguska event flattened 2,150 km² of forest, in a remote and sparsely populated region of the taiga.

probes.question: About how many square kilometres of forest did the Tunguska event flatten?
True or false: the Tunguska event happened in Central Siberia.

image_brief.show: Trees knocked down by the Tunguska blast, photographed in 1929

claims.quote: The Tunguska event was a large explosion that occurred on the morning of 30 June
at around 7:14 KRAT (0:14 UT ) in Central Siberia

claims.claim: It flattened 2,150 km² of forest (question, answer, reveal, probe 1)
claims.quote: Flattened 2,150 km (830 sq mi) of forest
claims.note: Page text lost the superscript but gives 830 sq mi; 830 x 2.59 = 2,149.7 km², so km² is right. Other passages say 'nearly' / 'more than' 2,150, so 'about' in the question is apt.

claims.claim: A remote and sparsely populated region of the taiga
claims.quote: This cataclysm occurred in a remote and sparsely populated region of the taiga
